intro_html: Rendang is what happens when curry stops being soup and becomes a rich, clingy, caramelized coat of coconut and spice on tender chicken. It takes patience, not skill. Each bowl delivers 41 grams of protein for about $2.28, which is a steal for one of the great dishes of Southeast Asia.
cost_closing_html: About $2.28 a bowl for rendang that a Malaysian restaurant would charge $16 for, if you can even find one nearby. Fourteen restaurant-grade dinners for the cost of two.
shop_smart: Chicken breast in the 6 pound pack came in around $2.23 a pound on our board. That single number is why this dish costs $2.28 instead of $5.
The lemongrass paste tube looks expensive but replaces a specialty store trip, keeps for months in the fridge, and covers this whole batch with room to spare.
Onions are the biggest produce line here, so buy the big bag. Six pounds ran about $6.84, roughly half the per-pound cost of buying them loose.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Blitz the onions, garlic, ginger, and lemongrass paste into a rough puree in a blender or food processor, working in batches.
Heat the vegetable oil in your big pot over medium and fry the puree 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until it darkens and the raw onion smell cooks off.
Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, garam masala, and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cubed chicken breast and stir to coat, then pour in the coconut milk and sugar and bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered 35 to 45 minutes, stirring more often near the end, until the sauce reduces to a thick, deep brown coat on the chicken. Confirm the chicken reads 165 F.
Season with salt and pepper. The sauce should cling, not pool.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number from step 1, and divide by 14. Portion that weight into each container and every bowl comes out at 585 calories and 41 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Hearty dinners for about $2.28 a bowl. This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.
